source.author: verg
source.text: Ut primum alatis tetigit magalia plantis, Aenean fundantem arces ac tecta novantem conspicit; atque illi stellatus iaspide fulva ensis erat, Tyrioque ardebat murice laena demissa ex umeris, dives quae munera Dido fecerat, et tenui telas discreverat auro.
source.text_original: Ut primum alatis tetigit magalia plantis, / Aenean fundantem arces ac tecta novantem / conspicit; atque illi stellatus iaspide fulva / ensis erat, Tyrioque ardebat murice laena / demissa ex umeris, dives quae munera Dido / fecerat, et tenui telas discreverat auro.
source.text_english: As soon as with winged feet she touched the huts, she sees Aeneas founding the citadel and renewing the buildings; and on him was a sword starred with yellow jasper, and from his shoulders hung a cloak blazing with Tyrian purple, rich gifts that Dido had made, and had interwoven the web with fine gold.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: nunc ille dies det Iuppiter oro, ille super, quo te Scythici regisque marisque victorem atque umeros ardentem vellere rapto accipiam cedamque tuae mea facta iuventae.
reuse.text_original: nunc ille dies (det Iuppiter oro), / ille super, quo te Scythici regisque marisque / victorem atque umeros ardentem vellere rapto / accipiam cedamque tuae mea facta iuventae.
reuse.text_english: Now may Jupiter grant, I pray, that day, that day above all, on which I may receive you as victor over the Scythian, the king, and the sea, your shoulders blazing with the stolen fleece, and may I yield to your youthful deeds.
